documents.title: Adapter algebra (v0.71.34)
documents.description: Adapter algebra (v0.71.34) — soup adapters arithmetic "coder + 0.5*math - toxic" --adapter name=path -o out/ applies task arithmetic (arXiv:2212.04089) to LoRA deltas: add to blend skills, scale to dial one down, negate to subtract one. Because a LoRA stores factors whose product is the delta (ΔW = B@A), a naive coefficient scales the delta by c², making negation a no-op; Soup splits the coefficient as √|c| across the factors and carries the sign so ΔW scales linearly (verified: ||ΔW(2·a)||/||ΔW(a)|| = 2.000). That exactness is on the self (diagonal) term, so single-adapter scale/negate is exact while a multi-adapter sum also carries cross-terms. As of v0.72.0 mixed ranks are exact rather than refused: stacking the A factors and the scaled B factors reproduces the sum of deltas by construction, and --rank N truncates with an SVD only if you want a fixed output rank. Same-base check (--allow-cross-base), backdoor-scan gate (--allow-unscanned), hand-written parser with no eval. Honest scope: the mechanism (the delta really negates) is proven; the behavioural outcome, e.g. whether subtracting a toxicity adapter measurably reduces toxicity on a real safety eval, is not yet benchmarked.

documents.title: v0.75.1: an adapter with nothing in it, and eight hardening fixes
documents.description: Soup CLI v0.75.1, tagged 21 September 2026, is a security and correctness backport: the v0.75.0 tree plus 25 cherry-picks, written entirely by the maintainer, so unlike the three releases before it there is no contributor list. Four fixes mean something you already ran was lost. A layer-streamed LoRA adapter saved on peft 0.21 or newer is a 40-byte file holding zero tensors, because peft 0.21 selects tensors by prefixes read off named_modules() where 0.20 filtered by the lora_ substring, and the streaming wrapper's names carried .inner. while its state_dict keys were canonical; save_model, every save_steps checkpoint and get_peft_model_state_dict all returned nothing and nothing raised, and it cannot be recovered. Typing soup runs clean --keep-weights on Click 8.1 did the opposite and deleted whole non-best checkpoints. soup train --cloud modal lost its checkpoints with the ephemeral container. Ctrl+C during a Lambda submit could leave the paid instance running. It is also the fix for advisory GHSA-63h4-gvp4-r26g, rated high and covering eight issues across 0.7.0 to 0.75.0, with three credentials to rotate: the Hugging Face token was resolved for every hub and handed to ModelScope or Modelers, OPENAI_API_KEY went as a Bearer token to any https judge host, and credential option values were written to the audit log. Also: adapters verify --public-key accepted unsigned adapters even under --strict, the Web UI rendered dataset content as HTML with no CSP, soup serve tool routes checked neither Host nor Origin, MCP execution did not pin every approved input, and the config-regex guard ran the untrusted pattern to decide whether running it was safe.

documents.title: v0.73.0 "Borrowed Hardware"
documents.description: v0.73.0 "Borrowed Hardware" is the Soup CLI release that came out of three days on an 8x H100 box, the first hardware other than the 4 GB laptop every published number had been measured on. It found one silent correctness defect in layer streaming, four backends that had never actually run, and a documented multi-GPU entry point that had never launched. Read the re-run list first: a supervised run with data.max_length above 1024 was silently truncated to 1024 tokens with no warning, use_fsdp2_compile wrote an adapter that reloads as all zeros while the run exited 0 with a healthy loss, a streamed 32B or larger model in NF4 had wrong gradients, every soup ship verdict is suspect because two of three behavioural suites scored 0.000 on a model that does both tasks correctly and the refusal detector missed the typographic apostrophe, and a quantised GGUF export deleted a previously exported f16. The NF4 gradient defect (#331) is repaired here: the threshold is bracketed at 163.8 to 171.5 MiB per decoder layer, so 32B and 72B but never 8B or 14B and never bf16, the cause is buffer aliasing rather than a race because bitsandbytes keeps the packed weight outside save_for_backward, and the repair is gated at 256/256 gradient tensors on a real 32B and 320/320 on a real 72B against a control that reproduced the defect, costing about 3% VRAM and 4% throughput. Two capabilities are new, both config keys rather than flags: training.seed and training.data_seed, and full fine-tuning as lora.r 0. Packaging: Python narrows to 3.10 through 3.12 because 3.13 resolved untested PyTorch wheels that crash before Soup runs, trl widens to below 0.29 behind a capability probe, and soup serve gains --max-model-len. The published 119.6 tok/s laptop figure was measured on v0.72.2 at 952 MHz, before the repair; a post-repair row from another RTX 3050 Laptop, taken at a different clock, was recorded in v0.76.0, and the two are not directly comparable.

documents.title: Validation on hardware we do not own
documents.description: Layer streaming validated on an 8x H100 80 GB box, the first hardware other than the 4 GB laptop it was built on, and the first able to hold a resident reference for a real model. Bit-exactness is two claims, not one: the forward (logits, torch.equal) is exact against a resident reference of matching numerics at 0.5B, 8B, 14B, 32B and 72B, while the backward (every LoRA gradient tensor) was exact at 8B and 14B and WRONG at 32B and 72B before the repair described here. That defect, issue #331, is NF4-only above roughly 165 MiB per decoder layer (bracketed between 163.8 exact and 171.5 broken), the forward stayed bit-exact and the loss matched a resident run to every digit while 62 of 64 layers had wrong gradients, and the cause is aliasing rather than a race: bitsandbytes keeps the packed weight outside save_for_backward, so gradient checkpointing cannot recompute it and the backward reads a buffer slot already refilled. Nothing Soup has published sits above that boundary, since 8B is 105 MiB per layer and 14B is 132, and both survive a 50-backward soak at exactly 0.0. Peak VRAM is flat in model size across a fourfold range: 3,397 MiB at 8B, 4,475 at 14B, 4,845 at 32B, and 7,411 at 72B. The published laptop headline reproduces on completely different hardware at a median 113.00 tok/s in the same 3.32 GB peak (the laptop figure it reproduces was measured on v0.72.2 at 952 MHz, before the NF4 gradient repair; a post-repair row from another RTX 3050 Laptop, taken at a different clock, is recorded, and the two are not directly comparable), at a mean GPU utilisation of 54.1%; the transfer-bound explanation first given for that was retracted in August 2026, after an ablation measured the entire host-to-device term at 1.44% of the step, and the measurement itself is unchanged. Against DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 with CPU parameter offload at matched numerics on one GPU, streaming is 2.93x the throughput in 9.7x less VRAM, though the honest framing is not faster than DeepSpeed but built for a different situation. A streamed model converges indistinguishably from a resident one at this resolution: mean paired difference 0.0053 over five paired runs and 300 held-out items, smaller than either arm's own spread.

documents.title: v0.73.3: four flags that did nothing
documents.description: v0.73.3 is the first Soup CLI release the maintainer did not write: all 24 pull requests came from eight other people, five of them first-time contributors. What outside eyes found was four separate flags that the schema validated, the docs described, and nothing in the codebase read. training.bnb_4bit_use_double_quant changed a config fingerprint and nothing else; on Apple Silicon quantization 4bit was silently rewritten to none because device detection did not know MLX; soup train --no-reexec printed a launch command with your own flags missing, so following it trained without --fsdp and still succeeded; and data.interleave had no training-time reader at that release (filed rather than papered over, then wired in v0.74.0). Two more findings are the project's signature failure shape, a run that completes and is wrong anyway: assistant-only loss masking built its label mask from a tokenizer mapping's key strings, so a run trained on zero tokens behind a normal loss curve, and on Windows a process that exited with code 259 was indistinguishable from one still running and read as alive forever. The one new capability is soup mcp serve --allow-execute, which stopped reserving a gate and now runs a planned training or export behind a short-lived, single-use, server-generated confirmation token, taking the server from 16 tools to 18. No new measurement was made and no benchmark record was added.

documents.title: v0.73.1: the free GPU tier
documents.description: v0.73.1 repaired the GPU tier most people actually have. bf16 was assumed on every CUDA card, in fourteen places across twelve trainer wrappers plus the streaming setup and the supervised precision resolver, so every pre-Ampere card failed on every task and not only on layer streaming: a T4 on Colab's free tier, a T4 or P100 on Kaggle, and every V100, GTX 16xx and RTX 20xx ran in a dtype their GPU has no units for and said nothing about it. The trap recorded beside the fix is that the capability check counts emulation by default, so a T4 answers yes and the first attempt was a no-op on exactly the hardware it was written for. With the repair in, Llama-3.1-8B in NF4 streams on a free Colab T4 inside a process capped at 4.00 GB, with the cap shown to bite rather than assumed: measured peak 2.91 GB against a predicted 3.02, an over-prediction of 3.8%, seven steps, exit 0, an adapter with 128 of 128 tensors non-zero. No throughput is quoted from that run because a capped card is not a benchmark, and gradient exactness at 8B on a Turing card is not shown. The slot's own issue found the streaming VRAM pre-flight breaking its own contract that it never under-predicts: measured through the real soup train, it over-predicts by 8% at sequence 4352 and then under-predicts, 0.934x the real peak at 5120 and 0.787x at 6144, and the grid that validates it could not have caught this because all ten of its rows sit at sequence 256 or 512. Two new config keys, not CLI flags: training.stream_vram_probe measures one real forward and backward at your configured shape instead of predicting it, supervised fine-tuning only and off by default, and training.stream_vram_override replaces the free-VRAM figure the pre-flight checks against. Also: training.seed now reaches every trainer wrapper rather than one of eighteen, MLX adapters no longer save unresolved target modules that load as a silent no-op, backend mlx finally dispatches to MLX at all, and periodic checkpoints under use_fsdp2_compile stop loading as dead adapters.

documents.description: Layer streaming (BETA, v0.72.0; NF4 v0.72.2; breadth v0.72.3; preference losses v0.72.4) — fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B on a 4 GB laptop GPU, and align on the same card. The frozen base is never loaded resident: it is rewritten into one safetensors shard per decoder layer, held in CPU RAM (page-locked when the machine allows it), and copied one layer at a time into a small pool of pre-allocated VRAM buffers on a dedicated CUDA stream, so the next layer loads while the current one computes. Only the LoRA adapters, their gradients and optimizer state stay resident, so peak VRAM is bounded by ONE layer instead of the whole model, and quantization: 4bit shrinks that RAM store about fourfold. Measured on a 4 GB RTX 3050 Laptop at batch 1, S=512: Llama-3.1-8B 119.6 tok/s in 3.32 GB with the base page-locked at 3.60 GB and the GPU 100% busy (measured on v0.72.2 at 952 MHz, before the NF4 gradient repair; a post-repair row from another RTX 3050 Laptop, taken at a different clock, is recorded, and the two are not directly comparable), Qwen2.5-3B NF4 264.2 tok/s in 1.76 GB, and on the bf16 path 3B 143.1 tok/s in 2.15 GB where a resident run OOMs. Honest cost: 1.43x slower than resident, measured at 0.5B. Two config keys (training.stream_layers plus quantization: 4bit), not CLI flags, and a streamed NF4 run was bit-exact against a resident NF4 run in the v0.72.x gate (the v0.76.0 NF4 forward change has no exactness record of its own). Nothing above 8B is measured on this card, so no 14B claim for it; larger sizes were later validated on borrowed H100 hardware, where the streamed forward is exact against a resident reference to 72B and a gradient defect above roughly 165 MiB per NF4 layer was found and repaired. v0.72.3 widened the scope to nine architectures with real batches, gradient accumulation, resume, a VRAM pre-flight and an NVMe disk tier (rewritten in v0.76.0 as a background direct-I/O reader that can stripe across NVMe drives), and v0.72.4 opened it to the preference losses (dpo, orpo, simpo, kto) with DPO's reference model taken free from the same stream; v0.74.0 took the allowlist to ten with Qwen4-Exp text plus the Qwen3.5 aliases, and stopped keeping an untied embedding and LM head both resident; v0.77.0 took it to eleven with the DeepSeek-V3 family; what remains is transformers, text and plain LoRA. If you trained with streaming on v0.72.0, re-run that adapter: it was saved under keys that load as a no-op outside the streaming path, fixed in v0.72.1.

documents.title: LISA (v0.71.34)
documents.description: LISA (v0.71.34) — Layerwise Importance Sampled AdamW (arXiv:2403.17919), which reaches for full fine-tuning quality without a full fine-tune's memory. Measured at 3B and 8B on an H100, the quality half holds and the memory half does not: LISA beat full fine-tuning on held-out loss at both learning rates and trains an 8B on one 80 GB card where full fine-tuning OOMs at 73.94 GB, but it costs 1.22x LoRA's memory at 3B and 1.51x at 8B, widening with scale (both LoRA rows were measured before v0.74.0's fix for a frozen base loaded in fp32, so a LoRA run today needs less memory than they show; no repeat of the comparison is recorded), because embeddings, LM head and final norm stay trainable through every interval and are 70.7% of everything it trains at 8B. Where Spectrum picks layers once, LISA re-samples a small random set of decoder layers every N steps and freezes the rest, with embeddings, LM head and final norm always trainable, so peak optimizer memory is roughly embeddings + head + lisa_num_layers while the active set keeps moving across the depth of the model. Config: training.lisa_enabled (false), lisa_num_layers (2), lisa_interval_steps (20), lisa_reset_optimizer (true), lisa_train_embeddings (true); sft or pretrain (since v0.74.0) + transformers + text + quantization: none only, mutually exclusive with LoRA features, freeze_layers/freeze_ratio, Spectrum's unfrozen_parameters, train_router_only, expand_layers and moe_lora. documents.title: v0.74.0: the base was loaded in fp32 the whole time
documents.description: v0.74.0, tagged 4 September 2026, has no codename: upstream titled it with a sentence, the base was loaded in fp32 the whole time. 116 of its 120 merged pull requests came from somebody other than the maintainer, by 25 people. The headline is what a contributor found: a LoRA run freezes the base, the frozen base never receives an optimizer step, and all three supervised load paths passed no dtype at all, so a bf16 checkpoint was materialised at fp32. Measured on an H100 with Llama-3.1-8B and LoRA, peak memory falls from 48,241 MiB to 18,658 MiB, 2.59x and 28.9 GB, byte-identical across three repeats; the same defect stood in twelve more trainers, and a genuinely trainable base still loads fp32 deliberately. Nine further fixes mean a run you already finished was wrong: unknown config keys were silently dropped so a typo trained at the default, a sweep parameter matching no field ran a grid of identical arms and reported a winner, data.interleave had no training-time reader so every mixture trained on one dataset, MLX resume never matched its own checkpoints and restarted from scratch, six GRPO objective variants fell back to stock loss, quantize_reward_model was never read, use_cut_ce silently did nothing for a local checkpoint directory, soup ship judged an NF4 adapter against a bf16 base, and an LLM-judge gate divided a 1-to-5 rubric by 10. documents.title: The layer streaming paper
documents.description: The layer streaming preprint, version 3 (13 August 2026): Makazhan, A. (2026). Exact Layer Streaming: LoRA Fine-Tuning of an 8B Model on a 4 GB Laptop GPU (v3). Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0. Two DOIs that are not interchangeable: 10.5281/zenodo.21771064 is the concept DOI and always resolves to the newest version, while 10.5281/zenodo.21918325 is v3 specifically; cite the version you read, and v1 and v2 stay citable at their own version DOIs. The title and the claim are unchanged, still 8B on 4 GB, and no measured number has changed since v1. Version 3 retracts one explanation version 2 gave, that the method is bound by host-to-device transfer, after an ablation on the original laptop measured the entire host-to-device term at 1.44% of the step. Version 2 roughly doubled the paper (about 9,000 to about 19,800 words) with the 8x H100 session: the laptop result replicates at a median 113.00 tok/s in the same 3.32 GB peak, bit-exactness moves from three-layer fixtures to real sizes (forward 0.5B to 72B, backward 8B and 14B), trained-model quality is measured for the first time and is indistinguishable from a resident run, DeepSpeed is compared including the unflattering result that eight ZeRO-3 cards are slower than one card resident, and a silent wrong-gradient defect above roughly 165 MiB per NF4 layer is disclosed and repaired. Of v1's ten limitations, one is closed and four more narrowed, and seven new ones added. It reports two results on one RTX 3050 Laptop with 4 GB of VRAM: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in NF4 at 119.6 tok/s with a 3.32 GB peak at 100% SM occupancy (measured on v0.72.2 at 952 MHz, before the NF4 gradient repair; a post-repair row from another RTX 3050 Laptop, taken at a different clock, is recorded, and the two are not directly comparable), and Qwen2.5-3B with an un-quantized bf16 base at 143 tok/s in 2.15 GB, a configuration that raises CUDA out of memory when trained resident on the same card. Measured overhead against resident training is 1.43x at 0.5B, the only size that admits a valid resident baseline there. The published fine-tuning result for this hardware class was 1.3B, reached by LSP-Offload (arXiv:2406.10181) by compressing the optimisation rather than streaming the base, while the systems that do stream weights during training are evaluated on an H200 with 1.5 TB of host memory, an RTX 4090 with 256 GB, or a cluster. The contribution the paper defends hardest is not the throughput but the correctness protocol: because a severed autograd graph still yields a falling loss, the central check is bit-exactness against a resident reference of the same numerics (resident NF4 for a streamed NF4 run, never resident bf16), verified across nine architecture families in both precisions at 14 of 14 comparisons with a maximum absolute logit difference of 0.000e+00. It caught a PEFT dispatch path producing a 0.94 logit divergence with byte-identical weights and adapters, no crash and a healthy-looking loss curve. Three findings are independent of streaming: the cross-entropy logits term costs 14 bytes per element rather than the 6 first principles suggest, Windows and WDDM spill into host memory instead of raising out of memory so a completed run is not evidence that a configuration fits, and gradient accumulation is per-token I/O-neutral with a 2.52x opportunity cost against batch size. Includes the full limitations, the BibTeX entry, and the reproduction config.

Both are pure and offline and add no new trusted-exec surface. v0.71.40 also makes a comma-separated reward_fn train as an ensemble. documents.title: Seeds and reproducibility
documents.description: Seeds and reproducibility in Soup CLI. training.seed and training.data_seed are config keys, not CLI flags, and there is no --seed: seed covers weight initialisation of new parameters, data order and dropout, while the optional data_seed varies data order alone so initialisation stays fixed. Both default to unset rather than to 42, deliberately, because an unset seed has to reproduce two different historical defaults (42 for the trainer, 0 for the multipack sampler) and defaulting the field would have silently re-ordered every existing multipack run; an unset seed still resolves to 42 and a YAML true is refused by name rather than coerced to 1. Until v0.73.1 the key reached the supervised trainer and nothing else, so a seeded GRPO or DPO run was accepted, trained at 42, and said nothing, meaning replicates that differed only in their seed were the same run. It now reaches every wrapper and is applied before the model loads, because the adapter's own initialisation is drawn before the trainer's seeding used to happen; the values a run trains at are unchanged, what changed is when they arrive. What a seed does not buy you is stated plainly: it is not a determinism guarantee, since bit-exact reruns also need PyTorch's deterministic-algorithms switch which Soup does not set for you; a resident 4-bit run is still not bit-reproducible from a seed, diagnosed and not fixed; a streamed run is, at five runs to one adapter hash; and since v0.77.0 the MLX backend applies both, which it never did before. Why it matters for the release gate: three runs of one unchanged resident configuration moved two behavioural suites by 0.375 and 0.269 against a 0.05 regression threshold, so five of seven suites could cross the line on a re-run that changed nothing.

documents.title: v0.73.2: the release gate
documents.description: v0.73.2 stops the Soup CLI release gate lying in both directions. soup ship answers one question, did this model get better or did I break it, and two of its behavioural suites were ranking by the wrong thing. A stub answering every item correctly in the boxed-letter style scored 0.000 on mini_mmlu and mini_common_sense, and Llama-3.1-8B scored 0.423 on mini_mmlu, below a 0.5B, while scoring 1.000 on two other multiple-choice suites; both halves of the repair were required, since the extractor alone is worth eight items and the prompt change alone is worth zero, and together the same model moves 0.423 to 0.731. On mini_tool_call the 8B named the right tool 40 times out of 40 and scored 0.225 because it emitted three opening braces and two closing ones, and that suite now reads 1.000. A non-callable generator returned 0.0 rather than raising, so a caller's own mistake was indistinguishable from a regression and failed in the direction that looks like a finding. And a whole failure direction had no detector: a tune that refuses everything registered as a monotone safety improvement, so mini_over_refusal joins as the eighth bundled suite, 40 hand-authored benign requests scored as the fraction not refused. New CLI flag soup ship --noise-floor N re-runs the base N times and refuses to call a delta significant below what the instrument can resolve, because greedy decoding is not deterministic on a GPU: five runs of one model with no adapter spread 0.015 strict and 0.020 format-blind against a 0.05 threshold. Those two figures are the borrowed H100 session's, not this release's development box, which measured 0.0000 on CPU, and at n=3 with one model and one dataset the floor sizes the effect rather than calibrating a threshold. Read the re-run list first: any verdict issued before this release is suspect, and a --baseline snapshot taken before it is on a different scale for three suites.

documents.title: soup ship: the SHIP / DON'T-SHIP verdict (v0.71.25)
documents.description: soup ship — the one-command SHIP / DON'T-SHIP verdict for a fine-tune. Fuses leg 1 (the task metric strictly improved, via eval accuracy or an LLM judge) with leg 2 (no general benchmark regressed past a forgetting threshold, default 0.05 absolute points) into a single binary decision, refusing a model that wins the task but breaks general knowledge. One-screen reason, CI-gateable exit codes (0 = SHIP, 2 = DON'T SHIP, 1 = runtime error, 3 = usage error), offline --evidence path with no model load. New in v0.71.25; v0.71.31 adds --task-mode pairwise, a swap-debiased judge win-rate (base vs tuned per prompt); v0.77.0 adds --require-provenance, a strict offline drift check that compares the evidence's stamps with the adapter, task and source bytes, suite version and verdict policy.

documents.title: soup shrink: make a model smaller (v0.71.29)
documents.description: soup shrink (v0.71.29) — depth-prune a model + optional distill-heal, with a SHIP / DON'T-SHIP perplexity verdict. Implements 'The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers' (arXiv:2403.17887): ranks contiguous decoder-layer blocks by the angular distance the residual stream travels across them, drops the least-important block (first and last layers protected), then optionally distills the original into the pruned student via a LoRA subprocess and fuses the adapter back to one dense smaller model. Exit 0 = SHIP, 2 = DON'T SHIP, 1 = error. Arch allowlist v1: Llama / Qwen / SmolLM. Validated on SmolLM2-135M (drop 25% = 30 to 22 layers, ppl x2.98 unhealed; drop 4 + CPU heal recovered to x1.35).

documents.title: Preference losses over layer streaming (v0.72.4)
documents.description: Preference losses over layer streaming (v0.72.4). DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO now run against a base that never enters VRAM, so alignment stops being the step that forces a bigger card. The five accepted streaming tasks are exactly sft, dpo, orpo, simpo and kto; ipo, bco and the unified task: preference dispatcher are still refused, and grpo and ppo are excluded permanently because generation rollouts re-read every layer per token. DPO's reference model is the same streamed base with its LoRA adapters switched off, one set of weights and one RAM store rather than a second copy: measured on a 4 GB RTX 3050 Laptop with a 365M-parameter synthetic model (730 MB of weights), streamed DPO peaked at 81.87 MB against streamed SFT's 89.53 MB (0.914x) with a byte-identical store and buffer pool, while the control that forced a real second instance reached 812.32 MB, moving the peak by exactly one copy of the weights (730.44 MB). Read 0.914x as no second copy, not as a saving. The reference needs no second copy of the layer weights, but it is not free in time: DPO reads the layer stack 1.52x as often per step. KTO is not reference-free however it is usually described, and it requires batch_size of 2 or more because TRL's KL term is degenerate at batch 1. All four losses are bit-exact against a resident run of the same loss. No throughput figure is claimed for any preference loss because none was measured, and the VRAM pre-flight is a sound but loose upper bound that refuses DPO from max_length 768 on a 4 GB card with a 128k-vocabulary 1B model. On an untied checkpoint, dpo and kto also hold one private copy of the output head per step (v0.76.0), a documented cost the pre-flight charges.

documents.title: Scaling a streaming run (v0.72.3; disk tier rewritten in v0.76.0; DeepSeek-V3 and three opt-in keys in v0.77.0)
documents.description: Scaling a layer-streaming run (v0.72.3, widened in v0.74.0 and v0.77.0). Eleven architectures stream: llama, qwen2, qwen3, mistral, gemma, gemma2, gemma3_text, phi, phi3, qwen4_exp and, since v0.77.0, deepseek_v3 (the DeepSeek-V3 MoE family), plus the qwen3_5 dense and MoE aliases that route onto the qwen3 streamer; the six added in v0.72.3 were each verified bit-exact against the same checkpoint loaded resident under both bf16 and NF4 (multimodal gemma3 is refused; phi3 fuses Q/K/V into one qkv_proj and is bit-exact anyway). Batches above 1 and gradient accumulation both work, and at the same effective batch raising batch_size measured about 2.52x faster than accumulating, because accumulation re-reads the whole base per micro-batch while a real batch amortises it: on Qwen2.5-0.5B bf16 at seq 256, batch 1 runs 556.6 tok/s in 0.842 GB, batch 1 with accum 4 runs 540.1 tok/s in 0.846 GB, and batch 4 runs 1378.0 tok/s in 2.28 GB. A new pre-flight predicts peak VRAM and refuses a run that will not fit, because streaming bounds the weights but not the activations or the logits: on a 151,936-token vocabulary at batch 8 the logits tensor alone measured 8.71 GB, 146x the whole layer-buffer pool. Its per-logit constant was corrected from 6 bytes to a measured 14 and fitted to ten real runs with a worst error of 0.85%, never under-predicting any of them, though v0.73.1 later measured that contract failing at long sequence (0.934x the real peak at sequence 5120, 0.787x at 6144) because every row of that grid sits at sequence 256 or 512. Plus a throughput forecast from a GEMM ceiling measured on your own card in that session, --resume and --hf-resume unblocked by a load-side adapter-key fix, and an NVMe disk overflow tier (auto falls back, ram refuses, non-NVMe is refused outright) whose correctness is bit-exact against the RAM tier and whose reader was rewritten in v0.76.0 (a background direct-I/O thread, optional NVMe striping) and measured on one RTX 5070 Laptop 8 GB. The v0.74.0 additions carry weaker evidence than the original nine and the page says which: Qwen3.5 parity is against CPU resident controls, the 35B MoE run has no resident control at all, and Qwen4-Exp has a float32 tiny-model gate with real-checkpoint and NF4 validation pending, so it streams only with task: sft and quantization: none; deepseek_v3's forward and backward parity was gated on a tiny from-config model on CPU, with no real checkpoint compared against a resident run and no NF4 parity check.

documents.title: What's new across v0.71 to v0.77
documents.description: Everything that shipped across the Soup CLI v0.71 to v0.77 lines, newest first, each line naming the release it came from. v0.77.0: what v0.76 warned about is now refused, as the 31 staged fields, two deprecated config values and fourteen of the fifteen never-applied settings on upstream's list stop the load, Python moves to 3.11 to 3.13, AWQ and GPTQ export are removed, DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO train natively on Apple Silicon and layer streaming reaches the DeepSeek-V3 MoE family. v0.76.1: a maintainer patch in which the bundled DPO examples train again, every YAML file Soup reads gets nesting, expansion and size limits, the Typer floor rises to 0.15.4 and a Hub dataset id with a dot loads from the Hub. v0.76.0: settings Soup accepted and never applied now stop the load, with dozens of combinations that loaded on v0.75 now refused when a config loads (run soup doctor --config first), 29 staged fields that warned at load (refused since v0.77.0), and eleven gate commands moving to a 0 / 2 / 3 exit-code scheme. v0.75.2: a one-change security patch (advisory GHSA-9f49-hqpf-c849, rated medium) in which outbound endpoint checks refuse private IP literals over https as well as http. v0.75.1: a security and correctness backport carrying advisory GHSA-63h4-gvp4-r26g (rated high, eight issues, three credentials to rotate) and a fix for a layer-streamed adapter that saved with zero tensors on peft 0.21 or newer. v0.75.0: the same soup.yaml trained a different recipe on MLX than on CUDA, an unknown config key now refuses the load, validation loss is recorded on MLX (the transformers backend first evaluates its held-out split in v0.76.0) and torch moves to 2.6.0; all 60 of its pull requests came from outside the maintainer. v0.74.0: the frozen base was being loaded in fp32 on every supervised path and in twelve more trainers, worth 2.59x peak memory on an unchanged config, 116 of its 120 pull requests came from outside the maintainer, the stack moved to Transformers 5.16.1 with TRL 0.29 and PEFT 0.20, the free notebook tier could not stream at all until now, layer streaming reached a tenth architecture (an eleventh came in v0.77.0), and soup mcp serve gained bearer-gated sse and http transports. v0.73.3: every one of its 24 pull requests came from outside the maintainer, and they found four flags that were validated, documented and read by nothing, plus an MCP execution gate that stopped being reserved. v0.73.2: soup ship's release gate stops ranking by the wrong thing, mini_over_refusal joins as an eighth bundled suite, and --noise-floor measures what the instrument can resolve. v0.73.1: bf16 was assumed on every CUDA card in fourteen places, so the whole free notebook tier failed on every task, and the streaming VRAM pre-flight was caught under-predicting at long sequence. v0.73.0: three days on a borrowed 8x H100 box, which found a silent NF4 gradient defect above 32B and four backends that had never executed once. v0.72.4: DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO run over a streamed base, with DPO's reference model taken from that same stream with its adapters switched off so it needs no second copy of the layer weights (0.914x the supervised peak on a 365M synthetic fixture, against a forced second instance at +730.44 MB), free in memory but 1.52x the layer reads in time; the measurement records behind the whole line are published and the work has a preprint DOI. v0.72.3: soup doctor --disk reports the media type because the streaming disk tier needs NVMe and refuses SATA, spinning or unidentifiable media rather than guessing; the [mcp] extra is pinned below 2.0 after the SDK's 2.0.0 broke soup mcp serve on a fresh install; soup adapters arithmetic --rank N makes mixed-rank LoRA algebra exact instead of refused. v0.71: Reward Forge (soup reward synth synthesizes a deterministic verifier from your gold outputs and refuses a degenerate one, soup reward stress attacks it with empty, padded, repetitive and sentinel-spam junk), soup ship --emit-evidence plus a committed ShipConfig turning the verdict into CI for weights, the ship regression leg rescored over seven bundled offline suites, Data Moat II (dedup --semantic, data topics, data canary, train --replay), the compliance pack (hipaa, soc2, eu-ai-act and sr-11-7 templates, soup card, soup ci init), GGUF export validated end to end on Windows, LoRA task arithmetic, LISA, Whisper ASR fine-tuning, Online DPO, PRM-guided GRPO, soup shrink, soup mcp serve, the Fine-tune Doctor, closed-loop reward-hack mitigation, soup ship, a catalog that reached 142 recipes by the end of the line, and Spectrum targeted training. For the current flagship see the layer streaming pages.
